newsitem.title: KENYA: Red Cross envoy asks Sudan to free seized plane.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross envoy asks Sudan to free seized plane.

text.p: An envoy of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) is in Khartoum to press the authorities to release an ICRC plane a pro-government rebel group seized last week, an ICRC spokesman said on Sunday.
Th envoy, Paul Grossreider, is asking for the speedy release of the two pilots, a nurse, and five Sudanese patients, the spokesman for the ICRC's regional information office in Nairobi said.
The ICRC has rejected Sudanese allegations that the plane, which flew from northern Kenya to Wunruk in Sudan's Bahr el Ghazal province, was carrying arms and ammunition.
The plane was seized at Wunruk by a splinter group of Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) which backs the government's latest peace initiative in the war-torn south.
The main SPLA faction has rejected the peace initiative.
The spokesman said the plane's occupants were still being held, but were well.
He said ICRC's operations in Sudan would remain suspended until the plane was freed.
